title: JuiceBox offline in Enel X app
shortDescription: Station does not appear online in the app.
fullDescription:
JuiceBox relies on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. If the charger cannot reach the Enel X cloud, it shows offline in the app, though it can still charge. Very common after router changes or firmware updates.

Use the blue button on the charger to re-enter setup mode and reconnect Wi-Fi.

fixSteps.title: Hold blue button
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the JuiceBox blue button until it enters setup mode (fast blink).

fixSteps.title: Re-run setup
fixSteps.instruction: Use Enel X app → Add Device → follow flow.

title: Configuration failed during setup
fullDescription: First-time commissioning can fail if the phone loses connection to the JuiceBox's hotspot, or if the router security is not supported (WPA3 only). JuiceBox requires WPA2 on 2.4GHz.

fixSteps.title: Enable WPA2
fixSteps.instruction: Router → set 2.4GHz to WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed.

fixSteps.title: Re-run setup
fixSteps.instruction: Hold blue button, redo setup in app.

title: JuiceBox cannot detect connected vehicle
shortDescription: Connector plugged in but no pilot signal from car.
fullDescription: The pilot signal on the J1772 connector tells the charger a car is present. If the car's onboard charger or the connector pins are damaged, JuiceBox cannot start. Check connector pins for debris and try another car.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Look inside for bent pins or debris.

fixSteps.title: Try another car
fixSteps.instruction: If possible, try different vehicle to isolate.

faq.a: Yes — for all non-Tesla; Tesla needs adapter.

title: Firmware update did not complete
shortDescription: OTA update is stuck or repeatedly fails.
fullDescription:
Updates require a stable 2.4GHz Wi-Fi link for 10-15 minutes. If Wi-Fi drops, the charger restarts on old firmware and retries.

Move router closer or wire Ethernet if available.

fixSteps.title: Improve Wi-Fi
fixSteps.instruction: Move router or add repeater near JuiceBox.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Flip breaker 60 seconds to force retry.

faq.a: No — Enel X pushes mandatory updates.

title: Overtemperature protection
shortDescription: Unit overheated — throttled or shut off.
fullDescription:
JuiceBox throttles when internal temp exceeds ~70°C. Common in direct-sun installs or small enclosed spaces. Loose terminal connections also cause local heating.

Move unit to shaded, ventilated spot or have electrician verify torque.

title: Blinking red error LED
fullDescription: A blinking red LED is JuiceBox's generic fault indicator. Blink pattern maps to specific errors — see Enel X app for decoded fault. Common patterns: 2 blinks = GFCI, 3 blinks = ground, 4 blinks = overtemp.

fixSteps.title: Count blinks
fixSteps.instruction: Count blinks in one cycle to identify fault.

fixSteps.title: Check app
fixSteps.instruction: Enel X app shows decoded fault.

whenToCallPro: If fault persists after power cycle.

faq.a: No — solid or pulsing indicates charging.

title: Wi-Fi setup did not complete
shortDescription: Setup flow aborted before provisioning Wi-Fi.
fullDescription: Setup requires phone to temporarily join the JuiceBox hotspot, then hand off credentials. iPhones often drop the hotspot due to lack of internet. Turn off 'auto-join other networks' during setup.

title: GFCI protection tripped
fullDescription:
JuiceBox has a built-in 20mA GFCI that trips if leakage is detected between hot and ground. Moisture in the connector, a damaged vehicle inlet, or wiring issue in the panel trigger it.

Inspect the connector; if moisture is the cause, dry it and try again.

fixSteps.title: Electrician inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Verify wiring and ground if trips continue.

whenToCallPro: If moisture is not the cause.

title: Charge session will not start
shortDescription: Plugged in but no charging begins.
fullDescription: Sessions don't start when schedule blocks it, utility DR (demand response) event is active, or the car hasn't requested power. Check the app schedule and utility settings.

fixSteps.title: Check schedule
fixSteps.instruction: Enel X app → Schedule — disable if unwanted.

fixSteps.title: Wake car
fixSteps.instruction: Unlock and lock the vehicle to reinitiate.

faq.a: Utility demand response pauses charging during peak.

title: Enel X Way app error or crash
shortDescription: App does not show charger or crashes.
fullDescription:
The Enel X Way app is known for occasional backend outages after Enel's 2024 divestiture. If the app fails, the charger still works but you can't control schedules remotely.

Reinstall app or use ChargePoint app (JuiceBox has been integrated into ChargePoint roadmap).

fixSteps.title: Update app
fixSteps.instruction: App store → update Enel X Way.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall
fixSteps.instruction: Delete and reinstall; log in again.
